summary: This bill denies 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status to the Council on American-Islamic Relations and any similar organization found to have ties to terrorism, effective for tax years after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code but contains no provisions related to government expenditures, appropriations, or outlays. It has no bearing on spending levels.

Section 2 explicitly removes 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status from CAIR and similar organizations found to have ties to terrorism, making them subject to taxation. This directly alters tax treatment by increasing the tax burden on the affected entities rather than providing relief or lower taxes.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, providers, or coverage models.

No provisions address worker protections, unions, or employment policy.

The bill targets a specific religious-affiliated organization (CAIR) by removing its tax-exempt status due to alleged terrorism ties. While this touches on treatment of a religious group, it does not engage with the balance between religious exemptions and anti-discrimination rules; the focus is national security rather than religious liberty policy.
